title: Звонок в машине  (A Call in the Car)

segments.t: Now Arkady is in his official car, and his driver, Vitalik, is taking him through town. Last time, Samson went through with the humiliating deal, and Arkady simply broke his promise and sent him off to the job centre. Now the phone rings: it's Arakelyan, a businessman who owes the mayor a large payment for the new shopping centre. Let's listen in Russian first.
Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
Это Аракелян. Я по поводу торгового центра.
Это хорошо, что готово. А то мы уже начали беспокоиться.
Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
Извините, вечером не могу. Я улетаю в Ереван.
Ну как же ты не вовремя! Где ты сейчас?
Ладно, будь там. Через десять минут буду.
Let's take it a line at a time. Arkady is in a hurry, as usual, and the first person to hear about it is his driver.
Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем?
'Vitalik, why are we going so slowly?' the term for 'we are going',
, implies by car or any vehicle. On foot it would be a different action word. Then one impatient word.
is built from meaning 'fast', with an ending that translates to 'more'. Just then, his phone rings.
, is a very common way to answer the phone, and it sounds a little official, just right for a mayor. The caller is polite.
, is the long one you use with people you don't call by a nickname. Then he says who he is and why he's calling.
'It's Arakelyan.' On the phone, you introduce yourself with the expression for 'this is',
'I'm calling about the shopping centre.' The phrase for 'about',
, translates to 'concerning', and the shopping centre takes the ending for 'of'. Now the important news.
'Everything is ready on my side.' Literally, 'at me, everything is ready', where the little word
means 'at'. He means the money is ready. The mayor gave him three days to pay, in an earlier scene. Arkady is pleased.
Это хорошо, что готово. А то мы уже начали беспокоиться.
'It's good that it's ready. We were starting to worry.' Notice Arkady uses which translates to 'we',
, as if he were speaking for the whole town hall. Then he proposes a time.
Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
'Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.' It begins with an action word for 'call',
, and the last word translates to 'for tomorrow'. But that doesn't suit Arakelyan.
Извините, вечером не могу. Я улетаю в Ереван.
'Sorry, I can't this evening. I'm flying to Yerevan.' which translates to 'flying',
, is built from a beginning that translates to 'away': flying away from here. He gives a reason.
translates to 'Mum', as they often say just 'Mum' where English says 'my mother'. And he suggests something else.
'Maybe we could meet now?' The opening term,
, translates to 'maybe', and the action word means 'we will meet'. A very natural way to suggest something. Arkady grumbles, but agrees.
Ну как же ты не вовремя!
'Your timing couldn't be worse!' Literally, 'how untimely you are!'. Notice that Arkady uses the casual word for 'you',
, while Arakelyan uses the polite one. That tells you who is the boss here.
'Where are you now?' The language omits the present action word for 'to be', connecting the term for 'where',
translates to 'I in', as it's the name of a café in town. Arkady makes up his mind.
'All right, stay there.' Literally, 'be there'. The word
is the command for the action word 'to be'.
'I'll be there in ten minutes.' the translation for 'in',
, is used when you count time forward. The last word translates to 'I will be'. In the present, the language has no 'am', but in the future you do need this action word.
'Fine. I'll be waiting for you.' Literally, 'I'm waiting for you', where meaning 'waiting',
, is used. And again, the polite word for 'you'. Now new orders for the driver.
'Vitalik, we're going to the Santa Fe.' The action word
translates to 'we are going' and is used for a plan that starts right now. The same action word we heard at the very beginning. Let's listen to the whole phone call once more.
Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
Это Аракелян. Я по поводу торгового центра.
Это хорошо, что готово. А то мы уже начали беспокоиться.
Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
Извините, вечером не могу. Я улетаю в Ереван.
Ну как же ты не вовремя! Где ты сейчас?
Ладно, будь там. Через десять минут буду.
And that's the end of the call. Keep an ear out for the phrase about being there in ten minutes; you'll use it more often than you think. Until next time!
